name: BACH_0107_FSIM_stain3
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Invasive (100%)** · Confident · Careful review

Single-class conformal set and MUSK agreement [F1]; neighbors split and the stain is simulated-degraded.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Invasive 100%, InSitu 0% | Dominant top class |
| Conformal set | {Invasive}, α=0.10 | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 1.00 / 92nd pct | Not flagged; fairly atypical |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Agrees |
| Similar cases | 2 of 5 Invasive | Weak neighbor support [F5] |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 8) · ↑ invasive · Above typical; highest-scoring invasive-associated concept here [F3] · Validated
- **Gland / tubule formation** (region 11) · ↑ invasive · Scarce here; concept model associates this with invasive [F4] · Weak
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (regions 9, 11) · ↑ invasive · Mildly above typical; small contribution · Validated
- **Dense lymphocytic infiltrate** (region 3) · context · Below typical; not used as a reason [F2] · Weak

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing top 3 regions cuts invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion effect 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0; not shown to reflect classifier. TILs (8/20) is Weak.

## Could be wrong if
- Simulated stain degradation (severity 3) and 92nd-percentile OOD distort the score.
- Three of five similar cases are InSitu, so an in situ component may be missed.

## Check on the slide
1. **Region 8:** confirm tumor cells infiltrating stroma, the strongest invasion-concept region.
2. **Regions 4, 5, 1:** highest heatmap contribution; confirm invasive carcinoma.
3. **Regions 3, 11:** lowest per-region invasive risk; look for duct-confined or benign tissue.
